author: OpenAxolotl maintainer (concept and Meshy generation), brought inside its budget in-repo by the project's headless Blender pipeline
tool: Meshy (image-to-3D), run by the maintainer OUTSIDE this repository, then reduced inside it by tools/decimate_model.py (headless Blender 4.0.2): the Draco-compressed export was decoded, coincident vertices welded, 2,002,284 triangles collapse-decimated to 20,000, the 2048 maps kept at their source resolution, and the result gated on two-way surface deviation and on open edges. Uploaded as reference/coral_cove/Coral_Cove_River_Bank.glb.
prompt: Generated by the maintainer in Meshy; the exact Meshy prompt is theirs and is not recorded in this repository. The dense source is kept in reference/coral_cove/ so the reduction can be re-run at any ratio. Four flat-topped rock shelves with pale sand caps, dressed with green weed, red and blue coral and a starfish. Uploaded as a river bank; what actually arrived reads as standable platform islands -- one large kidney-shaped shelf and three smaller ones -- which is a more useful shape for this game than a bank would have been. THE FOUR SHELVES ARE ONE MESH and float apart from each other, so the file cannot be used as a single platform. Splitting the loose parts is tracked work. Nothing references it yet: it ships as material for level builders, per the project's promise that contributors build out of these assets. Shipped at 20,000 triangles rather than the environment category's 200,000 ceiling, because what has to fit is the scene rather than the file; at that count the surface strays 0.14% of the bounding-box diagonal, well inside even the character-grade allowance, and a render at the shipped count shows the crowns, the sand caps and the coral dressing all intact.
licenseTerms: Meshy's terms of service govern the generated mesh and its maps; the maintainer generated the asset under their own Meshy account and contributed it to this repository. The in-repo Blender pass that reduces it is Apache-2.0 with the rest of the project, but it does not change the terms on the geometry it transforms. REVIEW NEEDED (REQ-021) before any redistribution that assumes a uniform Apache-2.0 grant over assets/: the project's promise to contributors is 'build your level out of our assets', which is a grant that cannot be made over geometry whose terms are someone else's.
